objective: Document the verified distinction between native DR24 HATS lightcurves and Zubercal recalibrated PSF photometry, and keep the Park primary-product requirement open until the approved dossier is confirmed.

previous_knowledge_consumed.detail: The DR24 HATS lightcurve collection is a native time-series product with one row per ZTF OID and nested epochs.
IRSA lists DR24 Objects/Lightcurves HATS separately from the Zubercal recalibrated PSF-photometry bulk download.
The dossier refers to Zubercal/recalibrated photometry; equivalence to DR24 HATS is not established.

expected_improvement: Prevent mislabeling native DR24 HATS photometry as Zubercal
Make the primary-product acceptance decision explicit

source_identity.before: DR24 HATS and Zubercal were referenced in project context without one consolidated decision record.
source_identity.after: Separate source products and separate adapter requirement documented.

park_contract.before: The approved primary photometry product was not explicitly resolved.
park_contract.after: Three contractual options recorded; confirmation remains open.

scientific_validity.reason: No HATS-versus-Zubercal parity or photometric comparison was performed.

measurement.trade_off: The proposed dual-track architecture avoids falsely treating one source product as another, but may add implementation work if Zubercal is mandatory.

evidence: IRSA HATS tutorial and ZTF product catalog reviewed.
No source data were acquired or compared in this documentation cycle.

root_causes: The current adapter points to the DR24 Lightcurves HATS collection, while the Park dossier names Zubercal/recalibrated photometry.
unresolved: The Park acceptance authority must confirm whether HATS is acceptable as primary, Zubercal is mandatory, or both are required.

findings: HATS and Zubercal are distinct source products.
ZTF OIDs are partitioned by filter, field and quadrant; they are not canonical astrophysical identities.
Source product identity must be explicit in data contracts and user-facing output.

open_blockers: Confirm the primary photometry product against the approved Park contract.
If Zubercal is mandatory, implement its dedicated adapter and time-series reconstruction with parity tests.
If both are required, define a frozen comparison dataset and photometric validation protocol.

knowledge_carried_forward: DR24 HATS remains the current raw lightcurve acquisition adapter.
Zubercal remains a separate source stream.
No equivalence claim and no baseline/model mapping is authorized.
